chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-001.proposition: The traditional maximal conception of God is incoherent because infinite power, knowledge, and intelligence would be impossible quantitative, non-extensive infinities.

orphanFallback.rationale: Huemer introduces this as his principal affirmative objection and grounds it in a taxonomy distinguishing possible extensive infinities from allegedly impossible quantitative magnitudes.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-006.proposition: Greatest-possible power cannot be merely finite because finite power admits indefinitely greater amounts, while the only upper bound would be the disputed infinite quantity.

orphanFallback.rationale: Independently of the earlier defense, the source supplies a freestanding magnitude argument: no finite amount of power is greatest because greater finite amounts remain possible.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-008.proposition: Excluding future free choices from divine foreknowledge does not avoid infinite cognition, because infinitely many mathematical, past, and present truths remain to be known and integrated.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source itself identifies the remaining determinate domains of truth and argues that their infinite information and integration requirements persist under restricted foreknowledge.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-010.proposition: Zeno-style spatial division describes an actual extensive infinity because infinitely many points and segments genuinely exist and are traversed, although traversal requires only finite power.

orphanFallback.rationale: Huemer directly grounds the claim in the existence of spatial points and segments, using it to distinguish coherent extensive infinity from the disputed quantitative infinity of power.

chunk-002:c002-04.proposition: A timeless God cannot change his mind, because being outside time while possessing successive incompatible intentions combines contradictory attributes.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source states a self-contained incompatibility between timelessness and changes of divine intention, so the same proposition can stand as an internal-coherence objection.

chunk-002:c002-05.proposition: The Christian incarnation challenges the claim that God cannot walk or marry, because Jesus is held to be God, was embodied, walked, and could have married.

orphanFallback.rationale: Huemer grounds the objection in the doctrinal identification of the embodied Jesus with God, providing a direct internal test of claims that bodily divine actions are logically impossible.

chunk-002:c002-08.proposition: Thomson's lamp does not require instantaneous events, because infinitely many switchings can each occupy a positive, diminishing interval while all occur within finite time.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source provides the complete constructive basis: each switching has nonzero duration, yet an infinite sequence of diminishing intervals fits within a bounded temporal interval.
